response.description: A count data item of the number of steps in the line of descent from a common ancestor for a multicellular organism.
response.label: number of generations of multicellular organism

response.description: A quality that inheres in a community.
response.label: quality of an ecological community

response.description: The number of different species represented in an ecological community.
response.label: community species richness

response.description: A process that leads to a change in the number of individuals (positive or negative) in a population.
response.label: population growth

response.description: A population process that leads to an increase in the numbers of individuals in a population following a logistic (S-shaped) curve. Generally occurs when the population has a carrying capacity in a particular habitat.
response.label: logistic population growth

response.description: A population growth process that leads to an exponential increase in the number of individuals in a population.
response.label: exponential population growth

response.description: The Shannon Index and Simpson Index are examples of ways in which species diversity is quantified.
response.label: community species diversity

response.description: A domestic group, or a number of domestic groups linked through descent (demonstrated or stipulated) from a common ancestor, marriage, or adoption.
response.label: family

response.description: A community species diversity metric that accounts for both the abundance and evenness of the species present quantified via the following formula: the negative sum of, the product of the proportion of species i relative to the total number of species (pi) multiplied by the natural logarithm of this proportion (ln pi).
response.label: Shannon diversity index

response.description: A community species diversity metric that is quantified via the following formula: the reciprocal of the sum of squared proportion of species i relative to the total number of species (pi).
response.label: Simpson diversity index

response.description: A community species diversity metric that is quantified via the following formula: the sum of squared proportion of species i relative to the total number of species (pi).
response.label: inverse Simpson diversity index

response.description: The density of seedlings in an ecological community or population, often measured as the number of seedlings per area.
response.label: seedling density

response.description: The density of plants in a population or organisms (a single species), often measured as the number of plants per area.
response.label: plant density of a population

response.description: The density of plants in an ecological community (multiple species), often measured as the number of plants per area.
response.label: plant density of an ecological community

response.description: The density of seedlings in a population or organisms (a single species), often measured as the number of seedlings per area.
response.label: seedling density of a population

response.description: The density of seedlings in an ecological community (multiple species), often measured as the number of plants per area.
response.label: seedling density of an ecological community

response.description: The number of parts of a particular type that the bearer entity has. This is a relational quality, and thus holds between two entities: the bearer of the quality, and the type of parts.
response.label: has number of

response.description: This term was originally named "presence". It has been renamed to reduce ambiguity. Consider annotating with the reciprocal relation,PATO:0001555, has_number_of. For example, rather than E=fin ray Q=count in organism C=10, say E=organism Q=has number of E2= fin ray C=10.
response.label: amount

response.description: An amount which is relatively high.
response.label: increased amount

response.description: An amount which is relatively low.
response.label: decreased amount
